hypothesis: Integrity: a DBA cannot update, delete or move a stored vote; a forged or unsigned ballot is rejected; chain verification passes
statement: The owner and an account with the DBA role had 10 of 10 UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE and MERGE statements refused each, where an ordinary copy of the table accepted them. 5 of 5 forged or unsigned ballots were rejected. The DBA could still INSERT 3 forged ballots; the tally counted none of them (6 counted, 3 rejected) and the chain verified over 1651 rows.

checks.name: the owner cannot update, delete, move, truncate or merge a stored vote
the DBA cannot update, delete, move, truncate or merge a stored vote
the stored ballots are byte for byte what they were
checks.detail: 6 ballots, 18 ciphertext rows and 6 seals compared

checks.name: negative control: on an ordinary copy of the table both accounts can update and delete
checks.detail: the refusals above come from the blockchain table, not from a missing privilege

checks.name: a forged or unsigned ballot is rejected by cast_ballot
chain verification passes on both tables, over every row they hold
checks.detail: DBMS_BLOCKCHAIN_TABLE.VERIFY_ROWS: 1651 of 1651 ciphertext rows, 549 of 549 seals

checks.name: the tally counts none of the ballots that the DBA inserted
the decrypted tally is the true result

notes: the DBA could INSERT 3 of 4 forged ballots directly into the blockchain tables: INSERT is what such a table allows
